items.meta_title: Add a Server to VpnHood! MANAGER | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: Add a server to VpnHood! MANAGER and have it install VpnHood! SERVER for you, over SSH or with one command on Linux or in Docker, then create its access keys.
items.title: Add a server
items.lead: Add a server to VpnHood! MANAGER, and MANAGER installs VpnHood! SERVER on it for you, or gives you the one command that does. The server then connects to MANAGER, which issues its access keys.
items.req_machine: A machine with a public IP address, running Linux on x64 or arm64, with root access. The install commands run through sudo, so it has to be on the machine even if you sign in as root.
items.req_port: TCP port [server_port] open, both in the machine's firewall and in your hosting provider's.
items.req_ssh: For MANAGER to install the server over SSH, the machine's SSH port open to MANAGER: [port_ssh], unless you changed it.
items.req_docker: For Docker, Docker with its compose plugin. The installer can install it for you on Ubuntu, Debian and the distributions based on them.
items.add_how: Open [manager_servers], select [manager_add], name the server and select [manager_create]. MANAGER then shows the ways to install it:
items.shot_alt: The ways VpnHood! MANAGER offers to install a new server
items.opt_ssh: [manager_install_ssh_password] or [manager_install_ssh_key]: give MANAGER the machine's address and an account with root access, and it signs in over SSH and installs the server itself. For a key, upload its file with [manager_upload_ssh_key].
items.opt_command: [manager_install_command]: run the command MANAGER shows on the machine. It is the standalone installer, with the settings that connect the server to MANAGER. Keep the command private: it holds the server's credentials.
items.opt_windows: [manager_install_windows]: run the command MANAGER shows in PowerShell on a Windows machine. Linux is recommended, though: Windows' NAT translates only IPv4, so only on Linux does the server handle IPv6 properly.
items.opt_manual: [manager_install_manual]: for a server you installed already. Save the settings MANAGER shows as [server_appsettings], then restart the server with [server_restart_linux].
items.docker_command: Choose [manager_install_command]. In the command MANAGER shows, change [installer_linux] to [installer_docker], then run it on the machine. It installs the server's container with the settings that connect it to MANAGER, and asks the question the standalone install with Docker asks.
items.docker_existing: For a container you created already, choose [manager_install_manual] instead. Save the settings MANAGER shows as [server_appsettings] on the host, then restart the container with [docker_restart].
items.status_desc: The server connects to MANAGER over HTTPS, at [manager_agent_host]. Once it does, its status changes from [manager_not_installed] to [manager_idle], and to [manager_active] while devices are connected. To see the install options again, open the server and select [manager_install], or [manager_reinstall] once it is installed.
items.keys_desc: Create the access keys for your devices under [manager_access_tokens]. Then install VpnHood! CLIENT on each device, add a key, and connect.
items.run_desc: A managed server is the same VpnHood! SERVER as a standalone one, so it runs, logs and updates itself the same way: see Start and stop the server, or Start, stop and check the server in Docker.
items.next_access_points: Set the addresses your server listens on and puts in its keys
items.next_domain: Give your servers your own domain with a trusted certificate
